verdict.rationale: The only relevant evidence is a community report that Steel publishes pricing, with a developer tier on both a pricing page and in the docs. That same report says the two figures disagree ($59 vs $99), which weakens the transparency the story asks for. Nothing in the pack shows per-task or per-browser-hour rates, or any documented rate or concurrency limits. missing for 10: first-party pricing documentation, per-task/per-browser-hour pricing details, consistent pricing across pages, documented rate limits, documented concurrency limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I can see transparent per-task or per-browser-hour pricing and documented rate/concurrency limits before committing

citations.quote: Pricing page for developers is $59, Pricing in docs for developers is $99
